sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 1997. A Reference Grammar of Mbay. Munich: Lincom Europa (LINCOM Studies in African Linguistics 14).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.45.90.12.10 (14))
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.45.90.12.10 (14)
sources.note: Closest-related Sara language with a full modern grammar and a phonology chapter; would give the Sara-group statement on tone and absence/presence of stress that Keegan's Mango notes presuppose (Mango is not Mbay: identity caveat).

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. n.d. Extended Bibliography, Sara-Bagirmi Languages Project. morkegbooks.com. 7 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliography only; lists Isaac & Johnson 2007 (SIL ESR 2007-015 survey of Bebot, Bedjond, Gor, Mango) and no Mango-specific phonology; does not list Khamis 1983.

sources.citation: Dodom Ndildongar Fidele, Loubeta Miclo, Gaston Altoloum & John M. Keegan. 2014. Lexique Mango (3e édition). Cuenca: Morkeg Books / The Sara Language Project. 127 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; French one-page introduction then the tone-marked lexicon; no phonology notes, no stress mention.

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 2014 [2012]. The Central Sara Languages (9th ed., April 2014). Cuenca: Morkeg Books / The Sara Language Project. 505 pp. Lexicons of Bebote, Gor, Gulay and Mango with English introductory notes on phonology and morphology.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. General 'Tone' section (p. 10, PDF p. 14): 'All of the Sara Languages have three even tones: high, mid and low'; tone-bearing units are vowels and final sonorants; complex tones on VV/VR. Mango-specific 'Notes on Phonology' (pp. 337-343, PDF p. 341 ff.) cover consonants, vowels, vowel patterns, sound changes and tone changes in verb paradigms only; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in a prosodic sense anywhere in the 505 pp.

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. n.d. [2014]. Transcription for the Sara Languages. Sara-Bagirmi Languages Project (morkegbooks.com). 10 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 5: 'All of the Sara Languages have three even tones: high, mid and low'; vowel length not significant; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Isaac, Kendall & Eric Johnson. 2007. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Language Varieties of the Doba Area of Chad: Bebot, Bedjond, Gor, and Mango. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2007-015. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: Only other Mango-specific publication; establishes Mango/Gor/Bedjond as one intelligible cluster (relevant to identity); a survey, so at most incidental phonological notes.

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 1996 [1995]. Sara Vowel System. Proceedings of the Sixth International Nilo-Saharan Linguistics Conference, Santa Monica 1995. Reposted on morkegbooks.com 2014. 23 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Vowel system and harmony only; no stress, accent or prominence statement.
No phonology; treats Bedjond, Gor and Mango as one mutually intelligible cluster; cites only Ethnologue and Isaac & Johnson 2007.
